source_text: $d_{\rm TV}(p,q)=\sup_A|p(A)-q(A)|=\tfrac12\sum_i|p_i-q_i|=\tfrac12\|p-q\|_1$ (densities: $\tfrac12\int|p-q|$; without densities, the supremum over events). It is a distance between laws, with values in $[0,1]$: for any $g$ with values in $[0,1]$, $|\mathbb E_pg-\mathbb E_qg|\le d_{\rm TV}(p,q)$, and $d_{\rm TV}$ is the smallest possible $\mathbb P(X\ne Y)$ over all ways of coupling $X\sim p$ with $Y\sim q$. Pinsker: with natural logarithms, $d_{\rm TV}(p,q)\le\sqrt{\mathrm{KL}(p\|q)/2}$, in either KL direction because $d_{\rm TV}$ is symmetric. (Proof idea: recording only whether the event $A=\{p\gt q\}$ occurs keeps $d_{\rm TV}$ unchanged and can only lower KL, so the two-point case suffices, a one-variable calculus inequality.)

hypotheses: Finite PMFs; every real test-function coordinate lies in[0,1].
reviewed_clauses.per_clause_reason: The statement contains actual Bochner integrals against both PMF measures. The finite integral formulas, signed zero-sum atom differences, and bounded coordinate weights derive the claimed expectation inequality. It is not a numerical or assumed-expectation statement.

reviewed_clauses.source_clause: Finite PMFs satisfy natural-log Pinsker, including canonical infinite divergence at missing support.
hypotheses: Finite PMFs; the square-root real form additionally assumes the actual canonical KL is finite.
reviewed_clauses.per_clause_reason: The event-indicator pushforward is proved to be the actual Bernoulli law. Mathlib canonical klDiv_map_le is used in the proof, so recording the attaining event can only lower KL. The squared ENNReal theorem preserves infinity; the finite square-root form is derived from it. The two-point scalar calculus proof uses true derivatives and convexity, not assumed Pinsker.

reviewed_clauses.source_clause: The literal strict event A={p>q} attains finite TV; recording this event leaves TV unchanged.
hypotheses: Finite PMFs. Atom inequality is strict q_i<p_i; equal atoms contribute zero.
reviewed_clauses.per_clause_reason: These new wrappers use exactly the source strict event, rather than leaving the earlier non-strict positive-event convention unstated. Its actual absolute event probability difference equals the original event supremum; the corresponding actual Bernoulli laws have identical TV. The generic indicator-law theorem identifies them with genuine pushforwards.

reviewed_clauses.per_clause_reason: The theorem constructs a nonempty actual event-difference set and a finite upper bound, preventing real sSup default-value artifacts. Its sSup is bounded between0 and1 for genuine probability measures.

reviewed_clauses.source_clause: Arbitrary probability measures satisfy natural-log Pinsker in either KL direction because their measurable-event TV is symmetric.
hypotheses: Arbitrary measurable space; genuine probability measures. Real square-root form is only for the respective finite KL direction; squared ENNReal forms include infinity.

Taking the genuine event supremum yields the general Pinsker theorem. The separate new generic symmetry wrapper justifies swapping KL directions, rather than citing only finite symmetry.
